I've been doing wheat-maize rotation on this land for over a decade. My 10.1 mu all runs the same cycle — wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, maize goes in after wheat harvest in June. Same fields, both seasons. That's how it works here in Quzhou.

**Wheat (October planting):** I'll use an improved variety like Jimai 22 — that's what most people around here plant, and I know how it performs on my soil. I'll do rotary tillage after the maize harvest because the stalks need to be turned under and my soil is compacted by then. I'll put down compound fertilizer as base before planting, then topdress with urea at jointing in spring. Three irrigations: the winter water to see it through frost, jointing water, and filling water. I spray herbicide once in the fall and do one fungicide pass in late spring when rust gets around. Expecting around 450 jin per mu if no late frosts.

**Maize (June planting):** I direct-seed right after wheat harvest — no time to waste, the season is short. Hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 or whatever the county supply station has in stock that year. No tillage, just straight into the stubble. Heavy urea topdress when plants are knee-high. Summer gets rain so I usually only need to pump twice from the well if it turns dry. One herbicide spray after emergence, one pesticide for corn borer. Expect around 550 jin per mu.

I'm not changing much from last year. What I've been doing works, costs are predictable, and I know how to manage problems when they come up.
